title: Balance Bridge

description: Balance the see-saw drawbridge over the castle moat! Stone blocks stand on each side: when both sides weigh the same, the bridge goes level and your helper walks across. Say if a sum is true, find the missing number, act out castle stories, and share blocks in pairs and rows. Every instruction is read aloud, so new readers can play too.
notes: Number Quest Launchpad Unit 4, The Balance Bridge (grades 1-2): a Kit 2 game on Oomba3D 1.1.0 in the Castle Quest theme 1.1.0 (daytime, ink outlines, gear button, graphics 'auto'), loaded with exactly kit2ImportMap() (tests/unit/balance-bridge.test.js checks the literal map). The castle, towers, walls, banners, trees, hills and yard things are the theme's own pieces round a moat (g.world.water); the bridge, its pier and the stone blocks are the game's own simple meshes. The bridge is a see-saw: a Rapier rigid body (g.physics(), Rapier 0.21.0) on a revolute joint with stops at about 7 degrees and a spring motor; a landing block gives it a real torque impulse. Which side is heavier comes from the game's own sums (the blocks are laid out by the game in stacks of five, never free bodies, so they can always be counted); if Rapier cannot start, the game's own spring turns the bridge (state().physics says 'rapier' or 'simple'). One small block is a ONE; a wide slab marked 10 is a TEN (numbers over 20). A block that was taken away stays as a pale ghost. Made for a child who is only starting to read: every instruction is short, shown and spoken through BRB.speak (voice role friendly; the speaker button says it again), numbers are big, and every answer is a big button. No timer, no lives, no fail state: a wrong number is tried on the bridge (its blocks drop in, the bridge shows too light or too heavy, they go again) with a spoken hint, a wrong True/Not true or Even/Odd wobbles the button and the bridge and gets a hint; then another try. Three chapters of six rounds, made by window.BalanceBridge.round(chapter, n, lap) (the block between /* balance-bridge:begin */ and /* balance-bridge:end */, pure, seeded from the round number; a replay lap gets new numbers). Every round is two sides, L and R, lists of terms ({ n }, { n, op: '-' }, { q: true } the number to find). equal (step 4.1; 1.OA.D.7, 1.OA.D.8): rounds 1-3 True or Not true with posts holding the bridge level until the answer (a sum and its total, 5 + 2 = 7; a number and a number, 6 = 6, or on odd laps a taking away with the equals sign first, 7 = 8 − 1; a sum on each side, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2), at least one true and one not true every lap; rounds 4-6 find the missing number (8 + ? = 11; 5 = ? − 3; 6 + 6 = ?, or on odd laps 8 + 4 = ? + 5). story (4.2; 1.OA.A.1, 2.OA.A.1): spoken stories about stones, acted out by the blocks: add to, take from (the blocks roll off into the moat), put together with one part to find, compare (how many more to match), all within 20; then how many more are needed within 100 (tens slabs), and a two-step story within 100. groups (4.3; 2.OA.C.3, 2.OA.C.4): rounds 1-2 odd or even, the blocks shared one to each side (an even number balances, an odd number leaves one over), one round of each; rounds 3-4 an even number as a double (10 = ? + ?); rounds 5-6 rows of blocks added as equal addends (3 rows of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12, up to 5 by 5). The player picks one of the theme's five adventurers as a helper; the helper waits on the bank at one end of the bridge (never in front of the blocks) and walks across when it is level. Lesson mode: BRB.params { chapter: equal | story | groups, lock: 1 } opens that chapter only; finishing its six rounds calls BRB.gameOver({ won: true }) once (the single call site), which completes the course step. With no parameters a picture menu offers the three chapters. Save: BRB.storage 'balance-bridge-v1' holds only which chapters are finished. Every step of a round (blocks landing, the bridge coming to rest, the walk, the pause) is run by the game loop, not by wall-clock timers. Layout: the camera backs off until the bridge fits between the words and the buttons; on a tall phone the helper stands at the near corner of the bank. Keyboard: every answer is a button (Tab, Enter, Space). A device without WebGL2 or import maps gets the site's 'needs a newer device' card. Words: English only (the I18N block, read by server/services/tts-lines.js for AI voices). Test handle: window.__bb (also window.__brbTest): state(), fast(), hero(id), act('answer', v), spot(), heroAt().
